**Dimitri Khundadze - Peace is the only essential condition that will facilitate economic development; Georgia is heading in the right direction with its improvisational policy**

12:17, 10.04.2026

Peace is the only essential condition that will facilitate economic development, stated Dimitri Khundadze, General Secretary of "People's Power."

While speaking about Georgia's role as one of the important players in the Middle Corridor, Dimitri Khundadze noted that the country's economic development will maintain its function as a regional leader.

According to him, achieving this is only possible under conditions of peace, as war and development are unimaginable together.

"Peace is a necessary condition for utilizing the country's transport capabilities. A few days ago, when the situation in the Middle East became extremely tense, only Georgia's airspace was congested on the transport-air map. This was a very small example within the larger picture of what I am saying—that peace is an essential condition for fulfilling the transit function.

How can a country join sanctions when you won't achieve any results from it, even for those requesting them? How do you imagine destroying the Russian economy with Georgian sanctions? Our opponents raise the issue that active steps must be taken to improve the social situation, pensions and salaries should increase, jobs should be created, tourism should develop, etc. They present their proposals directly in figures. For example, representatives of Gakharia's party introduced an initiative that the minimum wage should be 1,050 GEL. 'Lelo' raises the issue that the pension should increase to 1,000 GEL—and all this is supposed to happen against the backdrop of sanctions? In a war situation, this is simply unimaginable!

These are hypocritically noble statements. Some even let it slip that it is better for 'hot bombs' to be falling than for there to be peace in Georgia. Development and war—these two things are incompatible. It is a fact that Georgia is moving in the right direction with its improvisational policy. For comparison, in Ukraine today, no one is thinking about increasing pensions or building schools and kindergartens. In Ukraine, there is only one concern: for this or that family member to somehow survive. More than 10 million people have already become refugees, and the economy is destroyed.

In our case, the tourism indicator has increased over the last year. It was 4.4 billion in 2024, and in 2025, 4.7 was recorded. Investments are growing, and the country's economy has increased to nearly 100 billion. This is precisely where the opportunity lies for infrastructure to develop, for investments to come in, and for even more tourists. After that, it will be possible to increase pensions faster and create jobs with more intensity—they have increased by 40,000 recently. I am not saying everything is ideal; I am saying that in this extremely difficult period, with such a policy, we have not only maintained peace and avoided war, but we have managed to make things better in every direction than they were yesterday. But this is not enough, and we want even better," stated Dimitri Khundadze.
